images.author: CDC and NIAID; microscopy by CDC, colorization and visual effects by NIAID
images.why: Caption identifies a red measles virus particle in a colorized TEM. Strong single-particle focal point for a near-square card. Linked rendition is limited to 1024 px; download could not be independently verified.

images.author: CDC and NIAID; microscopy by CDC, colorization and visual effects by NIAID
images.why: Caption identifies a gold measles virus particle in a colorized TEM. Alternative palette with a clear central subject. Linked rendition is limited to 1024 px; download could not be independently verified.

images.author: CDC / Cynthia S. Goldsmith; William Bellini, Ph.D.
images.why: Caption confirms a colorized thin-section TEM of one measles virion, showing its nucleocapsid, envelope and surface projections. This is the low-resolution preview; the page advertises a 28.33 MB original whose direct URL could not be verified.

images.author: NIAID and CDC; microscopy by CDC, colorization by NIAID
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies hepatitis B virus particles colorized pink. Original-file candidate with particle detail suitable for cropping; the source caption and licence were verified, but the image download was inaccessible to the search tool.

images.author: NIAID and CDC; microscopy by CDC, colorization by NIAID
images.why: Caption identifies a TEM of hepatitis B particles colorized red and yellow; NIH also describes the blue background. Strong contrasting palette. Linked rendition is limited to 1024 px; download could not be independently verified.

images.author: CDC / Dr. Erskine Palmer
images.why: Caption confirms orange hepatitis B particles, explicitly identifying the round 42 nm virions as Dane particles. Low-resolution preview; the page advertises a 9.35 MB original whose direct URL could not be verified.

images.source: U.S. Geological Survey, reproducing CDC microscopy
images.author: CDC / Dr. Erskine Palmer; photo credit Bryon Skinner
images.why: Caption confirms a colorized TEM of intact, double-shelled rotavirus particles with textured capsids. Repeated particles allow flexible 9:10 cropping. URL comes from the page's Original download link; pixel dimensions were not independently verified.
